title: INSERT INTO SELECT
description: Learn how to use INSERT INTO SELECT to copy data from one table into another.

INSERT INTO SELECT Syntax

data.title: INSERT INTO SELECT Syntax
data.content: Inserts rows from a SELECT query into the target table.

data.text: In this syntax:

items: The query is any valid SELECT statement that retrieves data from other tables. It must return values corresponding to the columns specified in the column_list.
The TOP clause is optional. It limits the number of rows to be inserted. Use the PERCENT option to insert a percentage of rows instead of an absolute number.
It is a best practice to always use the TOP clause with the ORDER BY clause to ensure deterministic results.

data.text: Insert All Rows from Another Table
The following example copies all addresses from the customers table into the addresses table.

data.title: Insert All Rows
data.content: Creates the addresses table and inserts all rows from customers.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE sales.addresses (
    address_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    street VARCHAR (255) NOT NULL,
    city VARCHAR (50),
    state VARCHAR (25),
    zip_code VARCHAR (5)
);    

INSERT INTO sales.addresses (street, city, state, zip_code) 
SELECT
    street,
    city,
    state,
    zip_code
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.alt: SQL Server INSERT INTO SELECT example output showing copied addresses

data.text: Insert Some Rows with a Condition
Use a WHERE clause in the SELECT query to filter which rows get inserted.

data.title: Insert Filtered Rows
data.content: Inserts only addresses from stores in Santa Cruz or Baldwin.
data.code:
INSERT INTO 
    sales.addresses (street, city, state, zip_code) 
SELECT
    street,
    city,
    state,
    zip_code
FROM
    sales.stores
WHERE
    city IN ('Santa Cruz', 'Baldwin')

data.text: Insert the Top N of Rows
Use INSERT TOP INTO SELECT to limit the number of rows inserted.

data.title: Insert Top 10 Rows
data.content: Deletes all rows from addresses, then inserts the top 10 customers sorted by name.
data.code:
TRUNCATE TABLE sales.addresses;

INSERT TOP (10) 
INTO sales.addresses (street, city, state, zip_code) 
SELECT
    street,
    city,
    state,
    zip_code
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.text: Insert the Top Percent of Rows

data.title: Insert Top 10 Percent of Rows
data.content: Inserts the top 10 percent of customers sorted by name into the addresses table.
data.code:
TRUNCATE TABLE sales.addresses;

INSERT TOP (10) PERCENT  
INTO sales.addresses (street, city, state, zip_code) 
SELECT
    street,
    city,
    state,
    zip_code
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.text: Key Takeaways

data.title: INSERT INTO SELECT Key Points
points: INSERT INTO SELECT copies rows from a SELECT query into a target table.
Use WHERE in the SELECT query to filter which rows get inserted.
Use TOP with ORDER BY for deterministic row selection.
The column list in INSERT must match the SELECT query output in count and order.

**Inconsistent Error Handling**: Mixing different error handling patterns makes code unpredictable and hard to debug.
